title: Find the Largest Area of Square Inside Two Rectangles
summary: Given n rectangles on a 2D plane with edges parallel to the x and y axes, represented by their bottom-left and top-right coordinates, determine the largest possible area of a square that can fit within the intersection of at least two rectangles.
statement: Given n rectangles on a 2D plane with edges parallel to the x and y axes, represented by their bottom-left and top-right coordinates, determine the largest possible area of a square that can fit within the intersection of at least two rectangles. Return 0 if no such square exists.
constraints: The two arrays describe at least two axis-aligned rectangles with positive width and height.
For every rectangle pair, a square may be placed anywhere inside their intersection.
Return the greatest possible square area, or zero when every pair has empty or line-only intersection.
hints: A square inside an axis-aligned intersection is limited by the smaller overlap dimension.
Enumerate rectangle pairs and compute their horizontal and vertical overlap lengths.
For each pair set side=min(right-left,top-bottom); if positive maximize side squared.
Every qualifying square belongs to some pair intersection, and a rectangle of width w and height h contains a square of side min(w,h).
editorial: Every qualifying square belongs to some pair intersection, and a rectangle of width w and height h contains a square of side min(w,h).

tests.explanation: The first two rectangles overlap in a one-by-one square; no pair permits a larger one.
The overlap is three units wide and three high, so the maximum square area is nine.
